statement_en: If $f \in L^1_{\text{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^m)$, then the following limit holds almost everywhere: $$\lim_{\begin{aligned}m(B)&\to 0 \\x \in B\end{aligned}}\frac{1}{m(B)}\int_{B} f(y)dy = f(x)$$ That is, almost every point is a Lebesgue point.
